description: We are a team of students from Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) and Multimedia University (MMU), passionate about applying artificial intelligence, machine learning, and technology to solve real-world challenges.
summary:
BurningView is a web application that turns two decades of satellite fire detections into one consistent burning activity calendar. MODIS and VIIRS count fires differently, so their records cannot be compared directly. We calibrate MODIS onto the VIIRS scale using the years when both sensors were operating, and test every fit by leaving one year out at a time: across ten regions of Malaysia and Indonesia the median error is 18.4%. The result is a single harmonized record from 2003 to 2025, detailed at 5 km for Malaysia and Indonesia and at 1 degree for 233 countries worldwide.

On a 3D satellite globe, users pick a place and a month to see where fire was detected, how that month compares with normal, and which periods are unusual. A forecast then estimates how much fire to expect and where, from recent history and the El Niño index, with its tested skill reported.

This gives fire managers, scientists and land managers a consistent picture of when and where burning happens, so they can anticipate critical periods and direct monitoring.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

BurningView is a web application that harmonizes MODIS and VIIRS active fire detections into one burning activity calendar. A user picks an area and a month and sees where fire was detected, how that month compares with its normal level, which periods are unusual, and what to expect next.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Cleaning. From the NASA FIRMS archive we keep vegetation fires only (type 0), drop low-confidence detections (MODIS confidence below 30, VIIRS "low"), remove duplicates and convert to local dates.

2. Counting. Hotspots are snapped to a 0.05-degree grid and counted as fire cell-days: a cell that burns on a given day counts once. This reduces the effect of VIIRS splitting one fire into many small pixels.

3. Harmonization. For each region, MODIS is calibrated onto the VIIRS scale over the months when both sensors were operating (from February 2012). We fit a linear model and a power-law model and keep the one with the lower error.

4. Validation. Every overlap year is predicted by a model fitted without that year. Across ten regions of Malaysia and Indonesia the median error is 18.4% per region-month (10.5 to 29.8% by region) and R-squared stays between 0.90 and 0.99.

5. Record. VIIRS is used where it exists and calibrated MODIS before that, giving one record from 2003 to 2025. A coarser 1-degree record covers 233 countries.

6. Anomaly. Each month is compared with the median of the same calendar month over 2003 to 2025.

7. Forecast. Expected fire activity combines recent years for that month with two climate drivers, the El Niño index (NOAA ONI) and the NASA GFWED drought code; each region keeps whichever wins its own backtest. Forecasts are issued at the end of May and scored on June to November without seeing the season: the typical monthly error is 42%, against 50% for the seasonal pattern alone. A second model estimates, for each grid cell, the chance of at least one fire day; tested on 2016 to 2025 its ranking skill (AUC) is 0.81, and the riskiest 10% of cells held 36% of all fire days.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Fire managers and early-warning teams get one consistent picture instead of two records that disagree. They can see when the fire season normally starts and peaks in their area, whether the current period is unusual, and which places to watch first. For Malaysia and Indonesia this supports haze preparedness, because fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan drive regional haze.

WHAT IS CREATIVE

- The calendar counts fire cell-days rather than raw hotspots, so the unit is closer to real burning than to sensor pixels.

- Each region gets its own calibration, chosen by held-out validation rather than assumed.

- Results are shown on a 3D satellite globe with real terrain, where users can move from the whole Earth down to a single district.

- Every number on the site comes with the check behind it, so users know how far to trust it.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

- Honesty about uncertainty: calibrated values before 2012 are estimates, and the error is reported.

- Known risk: the Terra and Aqua orbits have drifted since about 2022, which changes the time of day MODIS observes. The harmonized record after 2012 uses VIIRS, so this affects only the calibration fit.

- The global record is coarser than the regional one and uses one model for all countries, so the two should not be compared number for number.

- Forecasts are probabilities based on history and El Niño, not predictions of specific fires.

- Area names on the forecast map are approximate.

TOOLS

Python (pandas, NumPy, FastAPI, Uvicorn), JavaScript, HTML and CSS, MapLibre GL JS, Leaflet, Chart.js, WebGL, Git and GitHub Pages.
